companies._: Lead scoring. A company needs no vacancy to need a developer: segment, industry, size, stack and country decide.
companies._kindWeights: Weight by company kind. A startup without catalog tags otherwise scores almost zero and does not clear the threshold, even though it is worth writing to. Outstaff and product are penalized: the former has a middleman, the latter does not respond to cold outreach.
companies._stale: Penalty for a dead site. An agency with a copyright year from two years ago and no fresh posts is not hiring and will not reply, and a letter there is a wasted evening.
companies._hiring: The team is hiring developers right now (seen on a board in the last 45 days): it needs hands and might take a contractor.

reputation._: Reputation in the catalog. A studio with reviews genuinely works with clients, an empty card is often abandoned.

site._: Site audit for segments that buy sites. For them stack weights and the stale penalty are skipped: a Tilda clinic with a 2019 footer is a lead, not a dead company. Each audit issue adds perIssue, up to maxIssues. A fresh fast site on a modern platform has nothing to sell.

companies._openLead: An open tender with the deadline still ahead: explicit demand, the strongest signal.
companies._minLeadFit: A tender the model rated under this fit (0 to 100) does not count as an open tender. Unrated tenders count.
companies._namedContact: A named person with an email: the letter reaches someone who decides.

hourlyRateBonus._: An agency's rate hints at budget. Very cheap ones will not pay, very expensive ones will not take outside work.

companies._web: YC and catalog tags that show whether this is a web product. The owner is a frontend developer, so SaaS and developer tools are his kind of work, while a robotics factory or biotech hires completely different people, and a letter there is pointless for both sides.
companies._industryWeights: By industry, lower case. Niches the owner sells to score higher; excluded ones go strongly negative.

queue._: The daily slice on the Leads page: how many companies, mixed across segments.
